basis: Sensorineural deafness, peripheral neuropathy and arterial stenosis define the syndrome; ocular findings lack evidence of common lasting damage.
Epilepsy arising from brain regions outside the temporal lobe.
Defined by impaired development of intellectual, motor or social functions; other organ abnormalities vary across subtypes.
Ketone transport disorder with ketoacidosis in 9/9; intellectual disability in 3/9 supports neurologic involvement at approximately 33%.
Abnormal breast lactation has no axis; hyperprolactinemia is a common underlying cause rather than an intrinsic diagnosis in every case.
Corneal protein deposition causes visual impairment and recurrent corneal erosion.
Defining abnormalities affect cerebral ventricles, radial bones and kidneys or urinary collecting systems.
Malignant epithelial-stromal tumor originates in the liver; intratumoral bone formation does not establish skeletal involvement.
Marrow failure and diabetes define the syndrome; nevi alone do not establish skin damage, and leukemia occurred in only 1/4.
Tumor originates in endocrine pancreatic delta cells despite lacking a hormonal syndrome; exocrine pancreatic involvement is not established.
Mitochondrial energy metabolism disorder with severe lactic acidosis; variable seizures, hypotonia and respiratory distress do not establish common organ damage.
Isolated focal or segmental dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease.
Localized fibroblastic neoplasm arises from the pleura.
Hereditary corticospinal tract disorder; renal, skin, endocrine and hearing abnormalities are subtype-specific rather than common across the umbrella.
Epilepsy caused by an antibody-mediated immune process.
Multiple cutaneous nodules and urinary tract malformations, including collecting-system duplication and hydronephrosis, define the syndrome.
Congenital pulmonary outflow atresia with right ventricular and tricuspid abnormalities; pulmonary refers to cardiovascular structures here.
GH/PRL-secreting pituitary tumor; direct acromegalic arthropathy and skeletal remodeling are very frequent (80–99%). Hypertension is a separate diagnosis.
Inherited retinal degeneration with rod-cone dystrophy, night blindness and progressive visual loss.
Lysosomal oligosaccharide storage disorders; developmental impairment or neurodegeneration affects most, and skeletal dysostosis exceeds ~30% across the group.
Glaucoma and sleep apnea with respiratory insufficiency define the syndrome; both are annotated as very frequent.
Ancestors establish an inborn glycosylation disorder; this poorly specified subtype has no supplied phenotype evidence supporting additional organs.
Congenital shortening of metacarpals and phalanges; cardiac abnormalities are confined to a subtype.
Gastroschisis variant with a congenital abdominal wall defect and herniation of bowel through the defect.
Limb defects, ectodermal dysplasia and orofacial clefting define EEC3; lacrimal duct stenosis in 6/6 supports ocular involvement. Renal and hearing frequencies are unestablished.
